title: Emotional Intelligence
description: Build practical emotional intelligence skills through five focused lessons and real-world practice.

lessons.title: Understanding Emotions
objectives: Explain understanding emotions in your own words.
Apply one practical step to your current situation.
body: Emotions provide information, rather than instructions. Notice body sensations, name your feeling precisely, and separate the event from your interpretation. You can feel disappointed and still choose a constructive response.

Practice focus: Understanding Emotions. Start with a real situation that is relevant to you, make one achievable change, and review the result. You can repeat this exercise as your circumstances change.
lessons.exercise: A colleague cancels a meeting. Write the event, your interpretation, the emotion, and an alternative explanation.

quiz.question: Which response separates an event from an interpretation?
options: They cancelled because they dislike me.
The meeting was cancelled. I feel disappointed and do not yet know why.
I should never feel disappointed.
quiz.explanation: A factual description leaves room for multiple explanations and a considered response.

quiz.question: What makes a useful practice plan?
options: A specific next step and a time to review it.
A promise to change everything immediately.
A fixed judgement about your ability.
quiz.explanation: Small observable steps make it easier to practise, learn, and adjust.

lessons.title: Empathy Development
objectives: Explain empathy development in your own words.
Apply one practical step to your current situation.
body: Empathy means trying to understand another person’s perspective without assuming you already know it. Listen without preparing your reply. Reflect what you heard, ask an open question, and check your understanding. You can understand someone without agreeing with every choice.
Practice focus: Empathy Development. Start with a real situation that is relevant to you, make one achievable change, and review the result. You can repeat this exercise as your circumstances change.
lessons.exercise: Write two open questions you could ask someone who is frustrated. Add a sentence reflecting their feelings without diagnosing them.

quiz.question: What best demonstrates empathy?
options: Immediately give advice.
Tell them their problem is small.
Ask what feels hardest and listen before suggesting solutions.
quiz.explanation: Listening and checking understanding respects the other person’s perspective.

quiz.question: What makes a useful practice plan?
options: A specific next step and a time to review it.
A promise to change everything immediately.
A fixed judgement about your ability.
quiz.explanation: Small observable steps make it easier to practise, learn, and adjust.

lessons.title: Emotion Regulation Techniques
objectives: Explain emotion regulation techniques in your own words.
Apply one practical step to your current situation.
body: Self-regulation creates time between a feeling and an action. Notice your trigger, pause, take a comfortable breath, and decide what you want the conversation to achieve. If safe, take a short break and agree a time to return. Regulation does not require denying or suppressing every emotion.

Practice focus: Emotion Regulation Techniques. Start with a real situation that is relevant to you, make one achievable change, and review the result. You can repeat this exercise as your circumstances change.
lessons.exercise: Describe a recent trigger. Create a pause plan with one physical cue, one safe action, and one constructive sentence.

quiz.question: When anger rises in a conversation, what is a useful next step?
options: Pause and agree to return when you can listen.
Send an insulting message immediately.
Pretend the problem will never matter.
quiz.explanation: A pause can reduce impulsive reactions while keeping a route back to the conversation.

quiz.question: What makes a useful practice plan?

lessons.title: Social Skills Enhancement
objectives: Explain social skills enhancement in your own words.
Apply one practical step to your current situation.

Practice focus: Social Skills Enhancement. Start with a real situation that is relevant to you, make one achievable change, and review the result. You can repeat this exercise as your circumstances change.

quiz.question: Which statement makes a clear respectful request?
options: You always ruin everything.
Could we confirm deadline changes in writing?
You should know what I want.
quiz.explanation: A specific request is actionable and avoids blaming someone’s character.

quiz.question: What makes a useful practice plan?

A fixed judgement about your ability.

lessons.title: Self-Reflection Practices
objectives: Explain self-reflection practices in your own words.
Apply one practical step to your current situation.
body: Reflection helps turn experience into a practice plan. Describe what happened, what you felt, what you chose, and what you might try next. Self-report is a learning aid, not a clinical test or a validated ability score. Track small behaviours you can practise, rather than labelling yourself good or bad.

quiz.question: What is the most useful reflection goal?
options: Become perfect at every relationship.
Never feel any difficult emotions.
Ask one clarifying question before responding in tomorrow’s meeting.
quiz.explanation: A specific, observable action makes practice and review possible.
